finding.claim: The /logo handler only checks that the user-supplied URL contains the substring "example.io", then fetches it. An attacker can use http://169.254.169.254/?x=example.io, http://example.io.evil.com/, or http://evil.com/example.io to make the server request internal or arbitrary hosts. The response body is returned to the caller, so this is a full-read SSRF. http.Get also follows redirects.
finding.sink: http.Get(raw) at main.go:36, with the response body copied to the client at main.go:38

trace.note: strings.Contains(raw, "example.io") is the only check; it is a substring test on the raw string, not a host check
http.Get(raw) with the default client, which follows redirects and has no IP restrictions
io.Copy(w, resp.Body) returns the fetched content to the attacker

finding.guards_checked: Only the strings.Contains substring check. There is no URL parsing, no scheme or host allow-list, no private-IP or DNS pinning, and no redirect restriction. The check is bypassable via the query string, path, userinfo, or subdomain.

verdict.guard_found: Only strings.Contains(raw, "example.io") at main.go:32, a substring check that does not close the finding. No URL parsing, host allow-list, or redirect restriction. The /cdn handler's strict host check does not apply to /logo.
verdict.reason: main.go:31 takes the attacker-controlled "logo" form value, main.go:32 only does a substring check, and main.go:36 calls http.Get(raw) with the default redirect-following client and main.go:38 returns the body to the caller, which is a full-read SSRF.
